lead.title: Open WebUI v0.13.4 ships Tether: your own computer becomes part of any instance
lead.summary: Released November 17, v0.13.4 introduces Tether, letting a personal machine plug directly into any Open WebUI instance — Ollama, LM Studio or OpenAI-compatible models, OpenAPI/MCP tool servers and terminals — without opening ports. The release also adds folder-sandboxed coding agents, native local MCP servers over stdio with no proxy, and more coding agents (Hermes, Antigravity, Copilot, Goose, Qwen Code) usable as chat models.

top_stories.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol
top_stories.summary: Astra targets hard professional and scientific work with new eval highs (+22 on ExploitBench for cyber tasks), while Sol is the efficient agentic workhorse; both ship in ChatGPT and the API at under a third of the prior Astra's per-task cost.

top_stories.title: Anthropic IPO: up to $88.5B raise with $26B tech-company private placement
top_stories.summary: The updated S-1 seeks up to $88.5B with a concurrent $26B placement committed by AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC; Amazon and Google would jointly own nearly 30% after conversion.

top_stories.title: Apple open-sources FastFrames video generation models on Hugging Face
top_stories.summary: FastFrames-L (14B) and FastFrames-S (1.3B) are open-weight video generation models at interactive latency, published as apple/FastFrames-L and apple/FastFrames-S.

top_stories.title: SGLang Consortium formed with NVIDIA, AMD, Google, Meta and Intel
top_stories.summary: The SGLang Summit closed with the five chip and cloud giants joining a new SGLang Consortium, with sessions on frontier models, agents and scale-out inference infrastructure.

items.title: Fine-tuning Gemma 4 edge models for MATLAB signal-processing code with SFT and QLoRA on a laptop iGPU
items.summary: Applies SFT and QLoRA to Gemma 4 E2B and E4B using only 66 checked examples on a laptop iGPU, showing small on-device models can be specialized offline for DSP code generation with clear error reductions.

items.title: Storing the Gemma 4 K=V cache once: exact global-KV savings in a paged serving engine
items.summary: Exploits the Gemma 4 31B global-attention design (value is the normalized key projection) to store the K=V cache once with unchanged attention kernels, confirming the reported up-to-37.5% KV-cache reduction.

items.title: Agentic on-policy distillation implicitly reshapes LLMs' ReAct patterns
items.summary: Across mathematics, ALFWorld and tau2-bench, on-policy distillation transfers capability while implicitly changing ReAct interaction patterns; general-reasoning supervision cuts mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4%.

items.title: MoE-LoRA for multilingual adaptation: a systematic empirical study
items.summary: Compares routed low-rank adapters for low-resource language support in LLMs and quantifies parameter-efficiency trade-offs of PEFT variants under a unified evaluation protocol.

items.title: The Kernel Reality Check: benchmarking and distilling efficient attention at scale
items.summary: A large-scale benchmark of kernelized O(N) attention versus softmax attention plus distillation of efficient attention, filling the missing fair-comparison baseline for linear-attention alternatives.

items.title: SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview: looped Transformer for long-context agentic work
items.summary: A 9B looped multimodal model (shared looped block + mHC residual streams) aimed at long-context and agentic workflows, Apache 2.0, with 13 community quantizations already on the Hub.

items.title: Qwen3.8-27B becomes the default local dense model
items.summary: The Apache 2.0 image-text-to-text model tops the trending list with 6.94M downloads, backed by a huge quant ecosystem (unsloth GGUF, nace-ai MLX packs with published KL/agreement comparisons).

items.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017: 763B open-weight MoE stays trending
items.summary: DeepSeek's MIT-licensed V4.1 Flash 1017 (about 763B params, multimodal) remains a top-trending open-weight release for local and self-hosted inference.

items.title: Show HN: Shard — distributed AI inference across multiple computers
items.summary: An open-source tool that splits LLM inference across several computers, letting modest local machines pool memory and compute to run larger models.

items.title: Show HN: OpenEye — Ollama-style runner for vision models with MCP server
items.summary: A local runtime dedicated to vision models such as YOLO, SAM 2 and depth estimators, shipped with an MCP server so agents can call them.

items.title: Show HN: Synapse — local code graph for AI IDEs, benchmarked against grep
items.summary: Builds a local code graph for AI IDEs and agent harnesses, positioned as a structured alternative to grep-based context retrieval with benchmarks.

items.title: Show HN: Machine Internet — turn a site's hidden JSON API into MCP tools
items.summary: Converts a website's hidden JSON APIs into MCP tools so local agents call structured data directly instead of scraping rendered HTML.

items.title: Show HN: TrnRT — open-source LLM inference engine for AWS Trainium
items.summary: An open-source inference engine targeting AWS Trainium chips, a self-managed alternative for local/private inference stacks on Trainium hardware.

items.title: Community patch starts DeepSeek V4.1 agent sessions 20x faster on a single gaming GPU
items.summary: A patched Strata implementation cuts DeepSeek V4.1 agent-session startup by 20x on a standard gaming GPU with no datacenter — a reproducible result for homelab agent workloads on consumer VRAM.

items.title: n8n 3.3.0 and 2.49.0 released with AI Agent node fixes
items.summary: Tool-call history is kept separate per input item, every tool-calling round of a turn is saved to chat memory, pre-tool model text is preserved in agent history, and custom OpenAI-compatible model IDs are accepted in v2.

items.title: r/LocalLLaMA debate: Sam Altman calls local inference 'a terrible allocation of scarce resources'
items.summary: A 6.4K-upvote thread dissects Altman's DRAM-utilization claim; the community counters that 24/7 home servers on cron and long tasks are well utilized, local inference cuts API bills, and data sovereignty favors your own box.

items.title: vLLM guide shows GLM-5.3 NVFP4 on two DGX Stations as NVIDIA's SC26 local-AI push continues
items.summary: The NVFP4 build of GLM-5.3 is served locally across two DGX Stations with tensor parallelism over two GB300 GPUs, MTP speculative decoding, FP8 KV cache and an OpenAI-compatible API.

items.title: Two cheap 16GB RTX 5060 Ti cards vs one RTX 5090 for local LLMs — tensor split nearly doubles per-dollar throughput
items.summary: XDA's bench in llama.cpp: tensor split on a $1,680 pair hit 79.6 tok/s on Qwen3-14B and 37.2 on Qwen3-32B versus 148.2 and 72.0 on a $3,200 5090, and the pair fits 32GB-class models that OOM on one card.

items.title: Project Maya runs 300-700B MoE models on a single GPU by tiering VRAM, RAM and SSD
items.summary: The open-source engine places hot experts in VRAM, next ones in RAM and the rest on SSD; a single RTX 3090 generated 26 tok/s on GLM-5.3-Flash (321B), with quantized builds from 73.4GB to 156.3GB for different memory budgets.

items.title: inferzero's Nov 17 release lifts Panther Lake (Arc B390) prompt speed from ~260 to ~550 tokens/s
items.summary: The Apache-2.0 engine for Intel Arc matches dedicated-Arc compute paths on Panther Lake and Lunar Lake, raising 27B 4K-prompt speed on Arc B390 to about 550 tok/s; Intel's own IPEX-LLM has been archived since January 2026.

items.title: Tom's Hardware GPU price index: AI memory orders keep squeezing consumer VRAM pricing
items.summary: The lowest-price tracker (last updated Nov 17) covers RTX 50/40, RX 9000/7000 and Arc SKUs amid an AI-driven surge, noting Nvidia purportedly allocates memory by profit per GB of VRAM, leaving the 32GB RTX 5090 above sane pricing.
